newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.Korea's Yukong to shut a reformer indefinitely.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Yukong to shut a reformer indefinitely.

text.p: Yukong Ltd, South Korea's largest refiner, plans to shut indefinitely a 15,000 barrels per day (bpd) reformer from Monday, a company source said on Friday.
The source said the shut down was being made because of losses from reforming -- a secondary refining process which converts naphtha into reformate.
Yukong has three other reforming units. The Yukong refinery has a crude processing capacity of 810,000 bpd and combined reforming capacity of 82,000 bpd.
Margins were bad but bearable in the first half, but in recent months they have become worse due to the high price of naptha, the source said.
He said the outlook for margins on reforming was gloomy and he did not expect a recovery any time soon.

Spot naphtha fob Singapore was assessed around $24.25 per barrel late on Thursday, while open-spec naphtha in Tokyo was assessed at $232.00 per tonne Friday delivered for first-half February and $227.00 for second-half February.
Reforming margins have been under pressure throughout Asia because of the high naphtha price and tight margin between naphtha and gasoline prices.
However, it is not always possible to close down reforming units because they produce hydrogen, which is used elsewhere in the refining process.
Most reforming capacity in South Korea is used for the production of BTX, an aromatic.
